messages:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 GPU capacity exhaustion detected in us-west-2. Autoscaler unable to attach new GPU nodegroups for the past 6m. Queue growth observed for inference-queue-prod. Pager triggered: PD-INC-4872. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/PD-INC-4872
erin_oncall: seeing it, joining. I can access the control plane. Initial triage: k8s autoscaler logs show repeated AttachRoleDenied errors.
maria_sre: confirmed — hitting attach policy limit and launch template version drift. Logs: `autoscaler: failed to create nodegroup: AttachRoleDenied: arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-gpu-attach`.
raj_platform: wtf — launch template was rolled yesterday for spot fallback, might have lost proper instance profile. Checking LT versions and nodegroup config now.
sam_support: customer impact — several customers reported degraded latency on embeddings and generation (api errors 429 + 503). Putting a quick stub in status page: "partial degraded serving in us-west-2; we're investigating".
jess_devex: adding prompt sets/evals owners. Any chance this is just throttling? metrics show token failures spike.
erin_oncall: timeline: queue growth started ~10:42 UTC. Autoscaler attempted scale from 60->95 nodes but stuck at 60. Nodegroup create attempts failing with IAM error.
maria_sre: snippet from kube-autoscaler: ```time="2026-03-15T10:48:12Z" level=error msg="failed to create ASG: AttachRoleDenied: not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRole for passed role" stack=....```
raj_platform: I see LT v3 was created but nodegroup still pinned to LT v1 in terraform. v1 uses old instance profile arn:aws:iam::123456789:instance-profile/redwood-gpu-profile. v3 uses updated profile name. The attachrole flow requires PassRole permission for the autoscaler IAM. Looks like the autoscaler's service account lost passrole after the RBAC rotation.
erin_oncall: immediate mitigation options?
ops_lead: list them — we need quick customer impact mitigation + permanent fix plan.
raj_platform: mitigation A: manually create nodes via eksctl with correct instanceProfile and bypass autoscaler for a short window. Mitigation B: patch the autoscaler IAM to include iam:PassRole to the new role — risk: IAM change in prod needs review but is fastest. Mitigation C: add temporary CPU-only pool and float workloads that tolerate CPU (not ideal for GPU inference).
sam_support: customers impacted: 12 tenants with high qps; estimated 18% of requests failing across us-west-2. I'll prepare a customer-facing blurb if we decide to run mitigation A or B.
maria_sre: I'm leaning B for speed — add iam:PassRole for role `arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-gpu-attach` to the autoscaler principal, then trigger nodegroup create. We can revert after.
erin_oncall: can we do a safe IAM tweak with a narrow resource+condition? e.g., limit to the LT ARNs and only for ec2:RunInstances/iam:PassRole.
raj_platform: yes — I'll craft a minimal policy and push via IaC. Pushing now to a hotpath change set: ```{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["iam:PassRole"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-gpu-attach"
}```
jess_devex: while iam change applied, we should also prepare manual node bootstrap commands in case autoscaler still misbehaves.
erin_oncall: raj — how long to apply IAM delta and validate?
raj_platform: ~3-5m to push policy and wait for propagation. Applying now.
incident_bot: Action logged: change submitted by raj_platform at 2026-03-15T10:53:02Z. Change set: iam-passrole-autoscaler-hotfix.
maria_sre: watch autoscaler logs. If it retries and succeeds we should see ASG/nodegroup creation events.
erin_oncall: monitoring cluster events...
(2m later)
raj_platform: IAM change accepted and propagated. Autoscaler started create attempts again. New error: `LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch` from EC2: the LT default version doesn't have the GPU nic changes. Need to point nodegroup to v3 or set version override.
maria_sre: ugh — so two separate drift issues: passrole + LT version. Autoscaler can still create ASG but EC2 rejects because launch template doesn't match expected instance profile?
raj_platform: correct. Quick path: we can create a new nodegroup with explicit LT version v3 using eksctl and the correct instance profile. That bypasses the nodegroup creation path the autoscaler uses but will bring nodes up quickly.
erin_oncall: do it. Take careful steps, annotate in thread. Keep me posted.
raj_platform: running eksctl create nodegroup --cluster=prod-usw2 --name=temp-gpu-attach-6123 --node-type=p4d.24xlarge --node-ami=custom --node-iam-instance-profile=redwood-gpu-profile --launch-template-version=3 --nodes-min=10 --nodes-max=40 --nodes=10

Command output: ```creating nodegroup "temp-gpu-attach-6123"...  (this may take a few minutes)```
incident_bot: Pager acknowledged by erin_oncall. Escalation timer paused.
maria_sre: while nodes spin up, let's cordon lower-priority GPU pods and move them to CPU pools if possible to free GPU slots. Use taint tolerations strategy.
jess_devex: running a short job to swap some backfill tasks to cpu-sim: `kubectl patch pod backfill-*-gpu -p '{"spec":{"tolerations":[],"nodeSelector":{"hardware":"cpu"}}}'` — will iterate safely.
erin_oncall: status update: nodes from temp-gpu-attach-6123 starting to register. 8/10 ready. Queue drain starting. Token failure rate dropping from 18% -> 7% now.
sam_support: updating customers: "We've routed around capacity shortfall in us-west-2; most requests are recovering, some may still see elevated latency. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary".
(10m later)
raj_platform: Nodegroup fully healthy: 10 nodes registered. Autoscaler now sees additional capacity and queue drained. Autoscaler reports 95->105 capacity updated.
erin_oncall: monitoring — 503s down to baseline. Customer error count trending down. Great.
maria_sre: root cause notes for postmortem: 1) IAM role passrole removed during RBAC/infra rotation; 2) launch template version drift because LT was updated in a separate deploy and nodegroup config wasn't updated; 3) autoscaler doesn't surface consolidated cause to SRE runbook.
ops_lead: we need immediate action items: A) revert/add precise iam:PassRole rule to autoscaler principal (raj to PR full fix) B) create a canary that validates LT versions vs nodegroup config pre-deploy (jess to own) C) update runbook for multi-failure autoscaler states (maria to own) D) consider a safety buffer of spare GPU nodes in us-west-2 for peak windows (ops_lead).
jess_devex: I'll add a pre-merge CI check that queries the LT default version matches terraform nodegroup version and fail if mismatch.
raj_platform: opening PR to add PassRole and include a narrow condition: `StringEquals: {"iam:ResourceTag/managed-by":"redwood-autoscaler"}` to limit scope. PR: https://git.redwood.example/infra/pull/5482
erin_oncall: going to transition to follow-up. Thanks team. I'll write up incident timeline and SLO impact metrics.
sam_support: draft customer follow-up: "On 2026-03-15 10:42 UTC we experienced GPU provisioning failures in us-west-2 due to infra configuration drift which caused autoscaler nodegroup creates to fail. We mitigated by creating a temporary nodegroup and applying a limited IAM fix. Impact: ~18% elevated error rate at peak for ~16 minutes, now resolved. Root cause and remediation steps will be shared".
maria_sre: adding final note: no data was exposed. This was capacity-only.
incident_bot: Incident PD-INC-4872 marked as resolved by erin_oncall at 2026-03-15T11:02:29Z. Postmortem assigned: PM-5678.
erin_oncall: closing thread, will post the full postmortem in #postmortems and link to this thread. Thanks everyone. :tada:"
